charts.title: 03_severe_9panel_engine_vs_sbml
charts.caption: Severe arm, all 9 observables, engine vs SBML extraction over 48 h. Inflammation (tissue integrity, blood pathogen) overlaps bit-for-bit; every divergence is in the hemodynamic layer. Dotted lines mark the SBP<100 / MAP<65 / HR>90 thresholds.
charts.interpretation: Severe arm, all 9 observables, engine vs SBML extraction over 48 h. Inflammation (tissue integrity, blood pathogen) overlaps bit-for-bit; every divergence is in the hemodynamic layer. Dotted lines mark the SBP<100 / MAP<65 / HR>90 thresholds.

charts.title: 04_severe_mechanism_co_svr
charts.caption: The two drive MAP down to ≈70 mmHg (still above the MAP<65 shock threshold at 48 h) by different routes: the engine declines via cardiac-output failure with near-constant SVR (hypodynamic/low-output), while the extraction holds output and swings SVR — vasoconstriction then sympathetic-fatigue vasodilation (hyperdynamic/warm). The extraction's single AIR→sympathetic arc overshoots the vasomotor response the engine's full cardiovascular control keeps muted.

charts.title: 05_severe_phase_portrait_co_svr
charts.caption: Severe sepsis (severity 3) plotted as a path in cardiac-output x vascular-resistance space rather than as two separate time series. Dots mark 6-hour intervals; the square is the shared healthy baseline (t=0), the stars are the 48 h endpoints, and grey dashes are iso-MAP contours (MAP = 17.34 x CO x SVR — a relation that holds to <0.5% in BOTH arms with the same constant). Both arms begin at the same point and finish on nearly the same low-MAP contour (~72 vs ~70 mmHg — both still above the MAP<65 shock threshold and still falling at 48 h), but by orthogonal routes: the real BioGears engine slides LEFT — cardiac output fails 5.8->4.5 L/min while SVR stays flat (cold, low-output decline) — whereas the SBML extraction slides DOWN — it holds/rebuilds output and lets SVR swing up then fall to 0.67 (warm, vasodilatory decline). The orthogonality is the finding: the extraction's single AIR->sympathetic arc overshoots the vasomotor axis that the engine's full cardiovascular control keeps muted, so the two approach the same low MAP by physiologically different routes. This is the geometric view of studies 03/05.
